topic: Natural Numbers, Whole Numbers, Integers and Rational Numbers
title: Natural, Whole, Integers and Rational Numbers
summary: Each new family of numbers answers a question the old one could not, and every family lives inside the next: N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q.

notes.title: 01 – Natural, Whole, Integers and Rational Numbers

keyPoints: **Q** = p/q with p, q integers and **q ≠ 0**.
N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q: every integer is rational (n = n/1).
5/0 is not a number; 0/5 = 0 is fine.

sections.h: Four families, one inside the next

blocks.alt: Nested boxes: natural numbers inside whole numbers inside integers inside rational numbers
blocks.caption: N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q.

head: Family
Set
The question it answers
rows: How many apples on an empty plate? Zero.
p/q, p and q integers, q ≠ 0
Half a pizza each for two friends? 1/2.

list: An integer n is rational because n = n/1 (5 = 5/1, −3 = −3/1).
Rationals can be positive, negative or zero: 3/4, −7/2, 0 = 0/5.
A rational number has many forms: 1/2 = 2/4 = 50/100.
Not every number is rational: √2 and π cannot be written as p/q (irrational, the next topic).

−4 is an integer and rational, but not whole or natural.
